::: {#sol-why-shrink}

Applying @sol-relu-grad's reasoning to $g$, then @sol-linear-input-grad, takes the gradient back one layer:

$$
\gradwrt{\vhidval_{\layeridx - 1}} L
= \tp{\matr{W}_{\layeridx}} \paren{g'(\vz_{\layeridx}) \odot \gradwrt{\vhidval_{\layeridx}} L},
$$

where $\odot$ multiplies entry by entry.
Each layer back multiplies the gradient by the slopes $g'(\vz_{\layeridx})$ and by $\tp{\matr{W}_{\layeridx}}$.
The [logistic function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-logistic-function)'s slope is at most $\frac{1}{4}$ ([lds's bound on it](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html#thm-logistic-derivative-bound)),
and less where units [saturate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-saturation),
so unless the weights are large, every layer shrinks the gradient by a factor less than 1,
and 10 layers multiply 10 such factors.
The ReLU's slope is 1 wherever a unit is positive,
so in @sol-deep-grad-norms the shrinking there comes from the weights alone,
which PyTorch starts small.

:::
